candidate_3_REFUTED_shared_output_vector.the_hypothesis: reports/c98 named this as a real asymmetry: handle_both_moves pushes phase-2 results into the same vector it pops phase-1 branches from, and every generate_instructions_from_move ends with combine_duplicate_instructions which REMOVES elements. segment() uses a fresh vector and never dedups across the phase boundary.
candidate_3_REFUTED_shared_output_vector.refutation: combine_duplicate_instructions (gen3/generate_instructions.rs:3138-3151) merges ONLY branches whose instruction_list compares EQUAL, and it merges them by SUMMING PERCENTAGES. The lists themselves are never altered. So dedup cannot make a pair-generated list unreproducible by composition -- whatever list survives the merge is a list one of the inputs already had.
candidate_3_REFUTED_shared_output_vector.so_the_asymmetry_is_real_and_inert: segment() not deduping means it may hold duplicate branches. It never means it holds DIFFERENT ones.

candidate_4_REFUTED_percentage_100.the_hypothesis: segment() feeds phase 2 `percentage: 100.0` instead of the phase-1 branch's real percentage, and branch emission is gated on `branch_ins.percentage != 0.0`, so the two can produce different branch SETS.
candidate_4_REFUTED_percentage_100.refutation: the direction is wrong. With 100.0 nothing underflows to zero, so segment() gets a SUPERSET of the branches the real percentage would yield. A superset cannot cause a prefix match to FAIL -- if the pair's list is in the smaller set it is in the larger one too. This candidate could only explain segment() finding a match the pair generation did not, which is the opposite of the observed failure.

candidate_5_the_one_the_evidence_points_.name: the second mover contributes NOTHING on the branch, because the first mover's move prevented it.
candidate_5_the_one_the_evidence_points_.why_prefer_it: 19000093/51 is Rock Slide against Hydro Pump. Rock Slide carries a 30% FLINCH chance in gen3, which is why that boundary has ELEVEN branches. On a flinch branch the second mover never acts, so the pair-generated `full` contains p1's phase and then goes straight to end-of-turn with no p2 action phase at all.
candidate_5_the_one_the_evidence_points_.the_mechanism: segment() requires a phase-2 continuation that is a prefix of `full` and at least as long as the phase-1 prefix. It regenerates p2's move from a state carrying p1's instructions -- including the FLINCH volatile -- so a correct regeneration should also produce nothing. Whether it does is the thing to check: if the regenerated phase-2 emits the move anyway, no candidate is a prefix and segment() returns None, which is exactly the observed failure and exactly on the branches carrying the majority mass (44%, 25%, 11%).
candidate_5_the_one_the_evidence_points_.why_it_fits_the_observed_split: the three voided branches hold ~85% of the mass while the three usable ones hold ~10%. A 30% flinch chance crossed with Hydro Pump's 80% accuracy produces exactly that kind of split, and the usable arms are the ones where both mons acted normally.
candidate_5_the_one_the_evidence_points_.the_decisive_check: replay 19000093/51 and print, per branch, whether the branch contains a p2 action phase at all. If the voided branches are the flinch branches, this is the cause. One instrumented run, no rebuild of the engine needed -- only the renderer's segment() needs a log line.
